title: Prompt-set cohort contracts, regression thresholds, and A/B rollback playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD-level specification for standardized cohort-based prompt-set contracts, concrete regression thresholds across signal classes, statistical A/B acceptance criteria, and automated rollback trigger definitions for the Optimize product. Purpose: create deterministic, actionable rules engineering and SRE can implement for canaries, canary->gradual rollouts, and emergency rollbacks.
background: Optimize currently relies on ad-hoc eval reports and manual judgement during canaries. Multiple teams have reported different tolerance levels and ambiguous stop/rollback criteria for regressions. This causes slow rollouts, inconsistent user experience, and occasional customer-facing regressions. We need a single canonical playbook that balances sensitivity to real regressions with robustness to noise, and that integrates with Console alerts and rollout automation.
goals: Define a small set of orthogonal evaluation signals (quality, latency, cost, safety) with clear measurement windows
Specify cohort sampling and prompt-set matrices that provide minimum statistical power for common effect sizes
Set per-signal regression thresholds and multi-signal decision logic for stop/rollback
Provide A/B acceptance rules for canary->rollout and a deterministic rollback playbook for automated enforcement
Produce deliverables consumable by engineering (alert thresholds, metric queries, runbook snippets) and PMs (sign-off checklist)
non_goals: Designing new model architectures or training pipelines
Replacing human review for nuanced safety cases (we will require manual escalation for ambiguous safety signals)
Building a full UI for rollout decisions (we will provide API/alert hooks first)
scope: Hosted and Dedicated deployment modes initially; Private deployments to be covered after pilot
Text generation and chat completion APIs; embeddings included for drift checks
Canary sizes: cohort-based (user cohorts + stratified prompt subsets) and traffic-based (1%, 5%, 20%)
Integration points: Console alerts, Rollout API, Optimize evaluation pipeline
promptset_sampling_matrix: Core prompt cohorts: 10 canonical customer intents (high-frequency), 20 long-tail prompts sampled by percentile frequency
Stratification: length buckets (<=64, 65-256, 257+), rhyme/format-sensitive templates, instruction vs. conversation
Sampling per canary: min N=500 responses per cohort per variant for quality signals, min N=2000 for aggregate latency/cost
Progressive sampling: initial canary uses canonical cohorts only; full rollout sampling includes long-tail and edge templates
evaluation_signals: Quality: human-rated pass@N and automated metrics (BLEU-like similarity, semantic embedding rank)
Safety: safety classifier + manual escalation for 'unknown' buckets
Latency: p50/p95 response time measured at token-level and end-to-end
Cost: per-token GPU-time and billing-estimate delta
Reliability: error rates (500s, timeouts), rate limiting hits
Drift: embedding cosine shift for canonical prompts and top-k user queries
regression_thresholds: Quality: cohort-level absolute drop >= 2.0 percentage points in human pass-rate AND relative drop >= 5% over baseline within a 24h window triggers a high-severity signal
Safety: any increase > 0.1 percentage points in 'unsafe' classifier positives is immediate stop for manual review
Latency: p95 increase > 200ms AND relative increase > 15% triggers rollback consideration
Cost: unit cost increase > 12% sustained for 6 hours triggers operator alert
Reliability: error-rate increase >= 0.5 percentage points or doubling of timeout rate triggers immediate mitigation
Drift: mean embedding cosine decrease > 0.08 for top-50 prompts across cohort over 48h is considered suspicious and requires gated rollout
ab_criteria: Primary metric selection: teams must declare 1 primary metric from evaluation_signals before canary start
Statistical test: two-sided bootstrap or permutation test with alpha=0.01 for primary metric, alpha=0.05 for secondary metrics
Power requirements: minimum 80% power to detect Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE); default MDE = 3% relative change for primary quality metric, configurable per project
Multiple comparisons: apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control across cohort buckets; require corrected p < 0.01 for acceptance
Effect consistency: acceptance requires primary metric non-inferior across >= 80% of canonical cohorts (non-inferiority margin = 1.5% absolute)
rollback_triggers: Automatic immediate rollback: any safety classifier delta > 0.1 percentage points OR catastrophic reliability failure (>=3x error-rate baseline)
Conditional rollback: if two or more orthogonal signals exceed their regression_thresholds within a 24h window (e.g., quality drop + latency spike), pause rollout and route to manual review
Gradual rollback: for cost or mild quality regressions (e.g., quality drop between 1.0-2.0 points), automatically cut traffic back by 50% and continue monitoring for 6 hours
Escalation flow: alerts created in Console with links to diffs, example failing prompts, and quick revert API. Pager escalation for P0 signals to SRE and product on-call
measurement_plan: All signals measured against a rolling 7-day baseline unless otherwise specified. Baselines updated weekly; for new model variants use pre-deployment snapshot baseline. Metric queries will be implemented as single-line SQL/PromQL snippets stored in the eval repo. All A/B tests must export raw per-event logs for re-computation and post-hoc analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Defined primary metric and cohorts in PRD and onboarding checklist
Automated alerts wired to Console with thresholds matching regression_thresholds
A/B test harness runs with required sample sizes and reports p-values, CIs, and cohort breakdowns
Runbook created describing automated rollback steps and manual escalation contacts
Sign-off by PM, SRE lead, and Safety reviewer recorded in ticket comments
deliverables: Specification doc (this ticket + expanded markdown) with exact metric queries
Alert definitions in Console and Terraform snippets for onboarding
A/B test checklist template for product teams
Runbook snippets and revert API contract for Engineering
Pilot rollout to two internal customers and post-mortem report

ENG-43321 (A/B logging pipeline): raw event export and storage

notes: Trade-offs discussed in kickoff: stricter thresholds reduce false negatives but increase rollbacks. We chose a conservative alpha (0.01) for primary metrics because production regressions have high cost. Safety signals short-circuit to manual review. For private deployments, customers can opt into a relaxed threshold policy with explicit SLA acknowledgement.
